readout_other: LFP power, phase-amplitude coupling, sample entropy, seizure firing rate (deep-learning detection)
direction_notes: Closed-loop TUS of the hippocampus reduced the seizure firing rate and LFP power and phase-amplitude coupling, and increased sample entropy, versus sham in penicillin-induced epileptic mice.
safety_notes: Authors state pressure, MI, calculated Isppa and temperature rise are below damage levels and cite a previous H&E study showing no damage; no safety assessment reported in this study.

timing.protocol_description: Closed loop: LFP segments identified by a deep learning model at 0.2 s intervals; on detecting a seizure signal a 5 s TUS (1 MHz, PRF 500 Hz, DC 50%, 0.33 MPa) was triggered, then recognition resumed and the cycle repeated. Open-loop comparison group received continuous 15 min TUS with the same parameters.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Each group consisted of five mice, comprising three males and two females.

Acoustic pressure 0.33 MPa, domain not stated.
Ten mice allocated to CTUS and Sham (five each); the open-loop OTUS group (n = 5) is compared with a previous study. Only the CTUS group is counted as sonicated.
Each triggered stimulation lasted 5 s; number and spacing depend on detected seizures.
